title: Halcyon 2.0 is live
description: Ten weeks with the Halcyon team, rebuilding the scheduling product around a single planning surface instead of four disconnected screens. Activation in the first quarter is up 38%.
pointOne: One planning canvas replaced the calendar, list, board, and timeline views
pointTwo: Onboarding cut from eleven steps to four
pointThree: Handover complete — Halcyon's two engineers now own the repository

title: We are booking from March
description: Two engagements at a time is still the rule, so the calendar has moved out. If you are planning something for spring, this is the month to talk.
pointOne: Two Build slots open in March and April
pointTwo: Strategy sprints can usually start within three weeks
pointThree: Partner seats are full until June

title: Ledgerly's brand, end to end
description: A four-week identity for a bookkeeping tool that had outgrown its first logo by about three years. Mark, type, colour, voice, and the templates their team uses weekly.
pointOne: New wordmark and mark, drawn from scratch
pointTwo: A colour system that survives dark mode and print
pointThree: Nine templates covering everything they actually make

title: Adaeze joins as brand designer
description: We have wanted a dedicated brand practice for two years and were waiting for the right person rather than the available one. Adaeze came from an editorial studio in Lagos.
pointOne: Brand engagements now run without a freelance bench
pointTwo: Identity work available as a standalone four-week block
pointThree: The studio is nine people, which is where it stays

title: Orbit Freight, six weeks flat
description: A quoting tool for a freight brokerage that had been running on a spreadsheet with 41 tabs. Kickoff to production in six weeks, exactly as quoted.
pointOne: Quote turnaround down from two hours to four minutes
pointTwo: The spreadsheet is archived, not migrated — the scope said so
pointThree: Built on infrastructure their one engineer can operate

title: We stopped writing specifications
description: After a year of quietly not reading our own documents, we replaced the spec with a one-page scope and a deployed URL every Friday. Projects got shorter.
pointOne: Scope documents capped at one page, permanently
pointTwo: Friday deploys from week two of every engagement
pointThree: Average project length down by nine days
